topic: A teacher shares study habits that beat re-reading. Ms. Okafor and her class are a made-up example.

slides.title: Read less, remember more
slides.subtitle: Four habits that work better than reading the chapter again.

slides.title: Re-reading feels like learning
slides.body: The page looks familiar the second time, so it feels known. But familiar is not the same as *remembered*. The test is simple: close the book. What can you write down?

slides.label: students scored higher after switching to self-tests
slides.note: Same chapters, same time spent. They closed the book and wrote down what they remembered.

items.title: Close the book
items.text: Write down everything you remember, then check.

items.title: Space it out
items.text: Review after one day, then three, then a week.

items.title: Explain it simply
items.text: Teach it to a friend in plain words.

items.title: Mix the topics
items.text: Switch subjects instead of one long block.

slides.quote: Struggling to remember is not failing. It is the moment you are learning.
slides.author: Ms. Okafor

slides.title: Close it, then write
slides.caption: Five minutes after each chapter is enough

slides.title: Try it tonight
slides.text: Pick one chapter. Read it once, close the book, and write down what you remember.
